cards.explanation: SageMaker Asynchronous Inference is designed for requests with large payloads and processing that can take minutes. It queues requests and manages endpoint scaling, avoiding the custom load balancing and container orchestration required by EC2 or ECS.

cards.q:
An ML engineer wants to use a set of survey responses as training data for an ML classifier. All the survey responses are either "yes" or "no."

The ML engineer needs to convert the responses into a feature that will produce better model training results. The ML engineer must not increase the dimensionality of the dataset.

Which methods will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
options: Binary encoding
Label encoding
One-hot encoding
Statistical imputation
Tokenization
cards.a: A. Binary encoding ; B. Label encoding
cards.explanation: Binary encoding and label encoding can map yes and no to a single numeric feature, preserving dimensionality. One-hot encoding adds columns, while imputation and tokenization do not perform the required binary categorical conversion.

cards.q:
An ML engineer must choose the appropriate Amazon SageMaker algorithm to solve specific AI problems.

Select the correct SageMaker built-in algorithm from the following list for each use case. Each algorithm should be selected one time.

• Random Cut Forest (RCF) algorithm • Semantic segmentation algorithm • Sequence-to-Sequence (seq2seq) algorithm
cards.a:
Summarize the text of a research paper. Seq2Seq
Scan every pixel of an image to help self-driving cars identify objects in their path. Semantic segmentation
Identify abnormal data points in a dataset. RCF
cards.explanation: Seq2Seq maps an input sequence to an output sequence for summarization. Semantic segmentation classifies every image pixel for scene understanding. Random Cut Forest detects anomalous points in unlabeled numeric data. The supplied choice order maps these tasks to indices 2, 1, and 0.

prompts.label: Summarize the text of a research paper.
Scan every pixel of an image to help self-driving cars identify objects in their path.
Identify abnormal data points in a dataset.

cards.q:
A company is planning to use an Amazon SageMaker prebuilt algorithm to create a recommendation model. The algorithm must be able to make predictions on high-dimensional sparse data.

Which SageMaker algorithm should the company choose for the recommendation model?
options: K-nearest neighbors (k-NN)
Factorization Machines
Principal component analysis (PCA)
Sequence-to-Sequence (seq2seq)
cards.a: B. Factorization Machines
cards.explanation: Factorization Machines model pairwise feature interactions efficiently in high-dimensional sparse datasets, which is a common recommendation setting. PCA reduces dimensions, k-NN compares neighbors, and seq2seq handles sequence transformations.

cards.q:
A company has several teams that have developed separate prediction models on their own laptops. The teams developed the models by using Python with scikit-learn and TensorFlow frameworks.

The company must rebuild the models and must integrate the models into an ML infrastructure that the company manages by using Amazon SageMaker. The company also must incorporate the models into a model registry.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: Export the models from the laptops to an Amazon S3 bucket. Use an Amazon API Gateway REST API and AWS Lambda functions with SageMaker endpoints to access the models. Register the models in the SageMaker Model Registry.
Import the models into the SageMaker Model Registry. Use SageMaker to run the imported models.

Use code from the laptops to create containers for the models. Use the bring your own container (BYOC) functionality of SageMaker to import and use the models. Register the models in the SageMaker Model Registry.
Import the Python-based models into SageMaker. Rebuild the scikit-learn and TensorFlow models in SageMaker. Register all the models in the SageMaker Model Registry.
cards.a: D. Import the Python-based models into SageMaker. Rebuild the scikit-learn and TensorFlow models in SageMaker. Register all the models in the SageMaker Model Registry.
cards.explanation: SageMaker includes managed scikit-learn and TensorFlow support, so the existing Python model code can be rebuilt with those framework containers and registered in Model Registry. A custom BYOC path adds container maintenance that is unnecessary for supported frameworks.

cards.topic: Large model training and real-time inference
cards.q:
A company is training a large language model (LLM) by using on-premises infrastructure. A live conversational engine uses the LLM to help customers find real-time insights in credit card data.

An ML engineer must implement a solution to train and deploy the LLM on Amazon SageMaker.

Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: Use SageMaker Training Compiler to train the LLM. Deploy the LLM by using SageMaker real-time inference.
Use SageMaker with deep learning containers for large model inference to train the LLM. Deploy the LLM by using SageMaker real-time inference.
Use SageMaker Notebook Jobs to train the LLM. Deploy the LLM by using SageMaker Asynchronous Inference.
Use SageMaker Studio to train the LLM. Deploy the LLM by using SageMaker batch transform.
cards.a: B. Use SageMaker with deep learning containers for large model inference to train the LLM. Deploy the LLM by using SageMaker real-time inference.
cards.explanation: SageMaker deep learning containers provide the frameworks and distributed tooling needed for large-model workloads, and large model inference containers support partitioned deployment behind real-time endpoints. Real-time inference matches the live conversational requirement.

cards.q:
A company has an existing Amazon SageMaker model (v1) on a production endpoint. The company develops a new model version (v2) and needs to test v2 in production before substituting v2 for v1.

The company needs to implement a solution to minimize the risk of v2 generating incorrect output in production. The solution must prevent any disruption of production traffic during the change to v2.

Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: Create a second production variant for v2. Assign 1% of the traffic to v2 and 99% of the traffic to v1. Collect all the output of v2 in an Amazon S3 bucket. If v2 performs as expected, switch all the traffic to v2.

Create a second production variant for v2. Assign 10% of the traffic to v2 and 90% of the traffic to v1. Collect all the output of v2 in an Amazon S3 bucket. If v2 performs as expected, switch all the traffic to v2.

Deploy v2 to a new endpoint. Turn on data capturing for the production endpoint. Write a script to pass 100% of input data to v2. If v2 performs as expected, deactivate the v1 endpoint and direct the traffic to v2.
Deploy v2 into a shadow variant that samples 100% of the inference requests. Collect all the output in an Amazon S3 bucket. If v2 performs as expected, promote v2 to production.
cards.a: D. Deploy v2 into a shadow variant that samples 100% of the inference requests. Collect all the output in an Amazon S3 bucket. If v2 performs as expected, promote v2 to production.
cards.explanation: A shadow variant can receive copies of 100% of production requests while all user-facing responses continue to come from v1. This enables representative v2 evaluation with no production traffic disruption before promotion.

cards.q:
A company is building an ML model by using Amazon SageMaker, AWS owned libraries, and open source libraries. The company must ensure that SageMaker does not collect metadata about usage and errors during training.

Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: Associate the SageMaker domain with a custom IAM role. Attach the role to a policy that denies Amazon CloudWatch service usage logs.
Add an IAM role to the SageMaker domain to deny Amazon CloudWatch the permission to report metadata.
Turn off the setting in the SageMaker domain to share metadata for console jobs. Opt out of metadata collection for each training job that is submitted through the AWS CLI or AWS SDKs.
Set a parameter to opt out of metadata collection for each training job that is submitted through the AWS CLI, Boto3, or the SageMaker Python SDK.
cards.a: D. Set a parameter to opt out of metadata collection for each training job that is submitted through the AWS CLI, Boto3, or the SageMaker Python SDK.
cards.explanation: Training jobs submitted through the AWS CLI, Boto3, or SageMaker Python SDK support a parameter that opts out of metadata collection. IAM denial of CloudWatch does not control this telemetry, and a domain console setting alone does not cover programmatic jobs.

cards.q:
An ML engineer is training an ML model to identify people's health risk based on 20 features and 1 target. The target class has two values:

• Likely to have health risk (positive class) • Unlikely to have health risk (negative class)

The age range of people in the dataset is 30 years old to 60 years old. Age is one of the features.

The ML engineer analyzes the features. For the positive class, the difference in proportions of labels (DPL) value is (+0.9) for the age range of 40 to 45 compared with all other age ranges.

What should the ML engineer do to correct this data imbalance?
options: Oversample the positive class for the age range of 40 to 45.
Undersample the positive class for the age range of 40 to 45.
Undersample the positive class for all age ranges except 40 to 45.
Oversample the negative class for all age ranges except 40 to 45.
cards.a: B. Undersample the positive class for the age range of 40 to 45.
cards.explanation: A DPL near +1 means the positive label is substantially overrepresented for the age 40 to 45 facet compared with the complement. Undersampling positive examples in that facet reduces its positive-label proportion and corrects the imbalance.

cards.q:
A company is building an Amazon SageMaker AI pipeline for an ML model. The pipeline uses distributed processing and training.

An ML engineer needs to encrypt network communication between instances that run distributed jobs. The ML engineer configures the distributed jobs to run in a private VPC.

What should the ML engineer do to meet the encryption requirement?
options: Enable network isolation.
Configure traffic encryption by using security groups.
Enable inter-container traffic encryption.
Enable VPC flow logs.
cards.a: C. Enable inter-container traffic encryption.
cards.explanation: SageMaker inter-container traffic encryption encrypts communication between compute instances in distributed training and processing jobs. A private VPC and security groups restrict reachability but do not themselves encrypt traffic.

cards.q:
An ML model is deployed in production. The model has performed well and has met its metric thresholds for months.

An ML engineer who is monitoring the model observes a sudden degradation. The performance metrics of the model are now below the thresholds.

What could be the cause of the performance degradation?
options: Lack of training data
Drift in production data distribution
Compute resource constraints
Model overfitting
cards.a: B. Drift in production data distribution
cards.explanation: A sudden decline after months of stable performance commonly indicates that the production feature or label distribution has shifted away from the training distribution. Overfitting and insufficient training data usually appear during evaluation, while compute constraints primarily affect latency or availability.

cards.q:
An ML engineer is using AWS Glue to transform proprietary data from a third-party vendor to a format that the ML engineer intends to use with the Amazon SageMaker DeepAR forecasting algorithm. The data includes several similar time series data files that the ML engineer must convert to the appropriate format. The ML engineer must compress the files to optimize storage costs.

Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: Use Snappy to convert the files to RecordIO-Protobuf and to compress the files.
Use XZ to convert the files to RecordIO-Protobuf and to compress the files.
Use XZ to convert the files to Apache Parquet format and to compress the files.
Use gzip to convert the files to Apache Parquet and to compress the files.
cards.a: D. Use gzip to convert the files to Apache Parquet and to compress the files.
cards.explanation: Apache Parquet is a columnar format that works well for analytics and compact storage, and gzip provides supported compression for the converted objects. The RecordIO-Protobuf choices do not match the Glue-oriented tabular conversion, and XZ is not the appropriate Parquet compression choice here.

cards.q:
A company has significantly increased the amount of data that is stored as .csv files in an Amazon S3 bucket. Data transformation scripts and queries are now taking much longer than they used to take.

An ML engineer must implement a solution to optimize the data for query performance.

Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: Configure an AWS Lambda function to split the .csv files into smaller objects in the S3 bucket.
Configure an AWS Glue job to drop columns that have string type values and to save the results to the S3 bucket.
Configure an AWS Glue extract, transform, and load (ETL) job to convert the .csv files to Apache Parquet format.
Configure an Amazon EMR cluster to process the data that is in the S3 bucket.
cards.a: C. Configure an AWS Glue extract, transform, and load (ETL) job to convert the .csv files to Apache Parquet format.
cards.explanation: An AWS Glue ETL job can convert CSV data to columnar Apache Parquet with managed scaling and little infrastructure work. Parquet reduces scanned data and accelerates analytical queries. Splitting CSV files or dropping all string columns does not provide equivalent optimization.

cards.q:
An ML engineer is analyzing a classification dataset before training a model in Amazon SageMaker AI. The ML engineer suspects that the dataset has a significant imbalance between class labels that could lead to biased model predictions. To confirm class imbalance, the ML engineer needs to select an appropriate pre-training bias metric.

Which metric will meet this requirement?
options: Mean square error (MSE)
Difference in proportions of labels (DPL)
Silhouette score
Structural similarity index measure (SSIM)
cards.a: B. Difference in proportions of labels (DPL)
cards.explanation: Difference in proportions of labels compares positive-label prevalence between a facet and its complement before training, directly exposing class or group imbalance. MSE evaluates regression error, silhouette score evaluates clustering, and SSIM compares image similarity.

cards.q:
An ML engineer uses one ML framework to train multiple ML models. The ML engineer needs to optimize the inference costs and host the models on Amazon SageMaker AI.
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
options: Create a multi-container inference endpoint for direct invocation.
Create a multi-model inference endpoint for all the models.
Create a multi-container inference endpoint for sequential invocation.
Create multiple single-model inference endpoint for each model.
cards.a: B. Create a multi-model inference endpoint for all the models.
cards.explanation: A multi-model endpoint lets models from the same framework share one endpoint fleet, reducing idle capacity and hosting cost.

cards.q:
A company is using an ML model to classify motion capture data from athletes. The company stores the data in Amazon DynamoDB tables. The ML model is deployed on an Amazon SageMaker AI endpoint. The model is retrained monthly based on any new data collected during the previous month.
The company needs to track and audit model drift, data drift, and feature attribution drift after each model retraining.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: Configure SageMaker Model Monitor to run on the SageMaker AI endpoint.
Use SageMaker Clarify to continuously monitor bias and feature importance.
Create an AWS Lambda function to run the SageMaker AI endpoint monitoring and store the results in an Amazon S3 bucket.
Implement an AWS Glue job to run data comparisons between the current model and the previous model.
cards.a: A. Configure SageMaker Model Monitor to run on the SageMaker AI endpoint.
cards.explanation: SageMaker Model Monitor provides managed schedules for data quality, model quality, bias, and feature attribution drift.

cards.q:
An ecommerce company trains an ML model to forecast future values based on time series data. The company needs to use the model to analyze sales data to predict future sales by product.
The company needs to train the model with the LEAST development effort.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: Use the Amazon SageMaker AI DeepAR algorithm.
Use the Amazon SageMaker AI XGBoost algorithm.
Use the Amazon SageMaker AI DeepAR algorithm with an LSTM architecture.
Use the Amazon SageMaker AI Neural Topic Model (NTM) algorithm.
cards.a: A. Use the Amazon SageMaker AI DeepAR algorithm.
cards.explanation: DeepAR is purpose-built for probabilistic forecasting across related time series and requires less custom development.

cards.q:
A logistics company has installed in-vehicle cameras for basic monitoring of its drivers. The company needs to implement a solution to detect driver behavior in real time, such as drowsiness and distraction, to prevent accidents.
Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST operational effort?
options: Use Amazon Rekognition eye gaze direction detection to monitor driver behavior and identify distractions.
Use Amazon SageMaker AI to customize an AI model to monitor driver behavior and detect drowsiness and distraction.
Integrate a third-party driver monitoring system with Amazon Rekognition to monitor driver behavior in real time.
Use Amazon Comprehend to analyze text-based driver feedback and identify distraction patterns.
cards.a: A. Use Amazon Rekognition eye gaze direction detection to monitor driver behavior and identify distractions.
cards.explanation: Amazon Rekognition exposes eye direction and eye-open attributes with low operational effort, although application logic is still needed to infer drowsiness.

cards.q:
A company has trained an ML model that is packaged in a container. The company will integrate the model with an existing Python web application. The company needs to host the model on AWS by using Kubernetes.
The company does not want to manage the control plane and must provision the resources in a repeatable manner. The infrastructure must be provisioned by using Python.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: Use AWS CloudFormation to provision Amazon EC2 instances that will create a Kubernetes cluster. Use Python scripts to deploy the container into the Kubernetes cluster.

Use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) to create a managed Kubernetes cluster. Use AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK) to provision the EKS cluster by using Python. Deploy the container in the cluster.
Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) to provision and manage the container. Use Terraform to provision the ECS service by using Python modules.
Use AWS Batch to provision and run the ML model as a batch job. Use the AWS SDK for Python (Boto3) to provision the cluster.
cards.a: B. Use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) to create a managed Kubernetes cluster. Use AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK) to provision the EKS cluster by using Python. Deploy the container in the cluster.
cards.explanation: Amazon EKS provides a managed Kubernetes control plane, and AWS CDK supports repeatable infrastructure definitions in Python. Amazon ECS is not Kubernetes.

cards.q:
An ML engineer is developing a linear regression ML model to predict house prices. The ML engineer has preprocessed the data and split it into a training set and a test set. The model performs well on the training data but poorly on the test data.
Which solution will address this issue MOST effectively?
options: Increase the complexity of the model to better fit the training data.
Apply regularization techniques to the model to reduce overfitting.
Increase the size of the training dataset.
Remove features from the dataset.
cards.a: B. Apply regularization techniques to the model to reduce overfitting.
cards.explanation: Strong training performance and weak test performance indicate overfitting. Regularization directly constrains the linear model.

cards.q:
A company is training a new ML model to replace a model that is deployed on an Amazon SageMaker AI real-time inference endpoint. The company wants to test the new model by routing a small amount of production traffic to it. The company must be able to roll back to the old model quickly if the new model performs poorly.
Which deployment strategy should the company use?
options: Perform a blue/green deployment with linear traffic shifting.
Perform a blue/green deployment with canary traffic shifting.
Perform a rolling deployment with a rolling batch size of 50% of the current fleet.
Perform shadow testing with a traffic sampling percentage of 100%.
cards.a: B. Perform a blue/green deployment with canary traffic shifting.
cards.explanation: Canary traffic shifting routes a small production share to the new fleet and supports quick rollback. Shadow responses are not served to users.

cards.q:
An ML engineer wants to use, prepare, and load data from Amazon S3 for analytics and ML by using Amazon SageMaker AI Studio.
Which SageMaker AI feature will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: SageMaker Data Wrangler
SageMaker Ground Truth
SageMaker Debugger
SageMaker Experiments
cards.a: A. SageMaker Data Wrangler
cards.explanation: SageMaker Data Wrangler imports, profiles, transforms, and exports S3 data from SageMaker Studio with minimal operational work.

cards.q:
An ML engineer is building an ML pipeline. The pipeline must process a dataset in two ways by using a single Amazon SageMaker AI processing job. The first step performs feature engineering and stores the result as tabular data. The second step transforms that tabular data into features that a model requires as training input.
The ML engineer must use a file format for the intermediate output that minimizes latency and maximizes throughput.
Which file format should the ML engineer use for the intermediate output?
options: CSV
Apache Parquet
Nested JSON
Deserialized JSON
cards.a: B. Apache Parquet
cards.explanation: Apache Parquet is compressed and columnar, which reduces I/O and improves analytical throughput compared with CSV or JSON.

cards.q:
A company uses an Amazon SageMaker AI ML model to make real-time inferences. The company has configured auto scaling for the Amazon EC2 instances that SageMaker AI uses for the inferences.
During times of peak usage, new instances launch before existing instances are fully ready. As a result, the model experiences inefficiencies and delays.
Which solution will optimize the scaling behavior?
options: Decrease the cooldown period for scaling policies to add instances more quickly.
Decrease the target value for SageMaker AI invocations per instance.
Enable SageMaker AI Inference Recommender to determine the optimal instance type.
Configure pre-warming of instances by using lifecycle configuration scripts for the SageMaker AI endpoint.
cards.a: B. Decrease the target value for SageMaker AI invocations per instance.
cards.explanation: Lowering the target invocations per instance causes scaling to begin earlier. A longer scale-out cooldown would be a more direct fix, but it is not offered, and lifecycle scripts cannot pre-warm endpoint instances.

cards.q:
A company deployed an Amazon SageMaker AI ML model to an endpoint by calling the CreateModel API operation. The SageMaker AI endpoint is in a private subnet of the company's VPC. The endpoint cannot reach the internet or any AWS services through the public internet. The company needs to access the model artifacts that are stored in Amazon S3.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: Create a NAT gateway. Configure the security group to allow outbound connections to Amazon S3.
Create a gateway VPC endpoint. Configure an endpoint policy that restricts access to the S3 bucket.
Create an interface VPC endpoint. Verify that the security group allows only inbound connections from the SageMaker AI endpoint.
Create a Gateway Load Balancer VPC endpoint. Configure an IAM policy that restricts access to the S3 bucket.
cards.a: B. Create a gateway VPC endpoint. Configure an endpoint policy that restricts access to the S3 bucket.
cards.explanation: An S3 gateway VPC endpoint provides private bucket access without NAT or public internet and supports a restrictive endpoint policy.

cards.q:
A company is developing a new ML model to rank customers by their propensity to buy a product. During exploratory data analysis (EDA), an ML engineer notices that the company has more data about current customers who have already purchased the product than customers who have not purchased the product.
The ML engineer needs to address this class imbalance before training the model.
Which solution will meet this requirement?
options: Apply Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) to the minority class.
Apply Principal Component Analysis (PCA) to the minority class.
Reduce features of the majority class.
Remove records from the majority class.
cards.a: A. Apply Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) to the minority class.
cards.explanation: SMOTE creates synthetic minority examples and directly addresses label imbalance before training.

cards.q:
An ML engineer is setting up an Amazon SageMaker AI domain with authentication that is managed by AWS IAM Identity Center. The ML engineer has already created user profiles in the SageMaker AI domain. The ML engineer needs to control what actions users can take based on their roles.
The ML engineer wants to assign pre-built roles and permissions to users to achieve this objective with the LEAST operational overhead.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: Create different IAM roles for each user. Assign different permissions to each role. Add each IAM role as a new user profile to the SageMaker AI domain.
Configure the SageMaker AI domain to use SageMaker AI spaces for resource isolation. Create IAM policies for each space. Assign the spaces to the corresponding user profiles.
Create permission sets in IAM Identity Center. Map the permission sets to the user profiles in the SageMaker AI domain.
Configure SageMaker AI roles by using IAM role-based access control. Assign roles directly to user profiles in IAM Identity Center.
cards.a: C. Create permission sets in IAM Identity Center. Map the permission sets to the user profiles in the SageMaker AI domain.
cards.explanation: IAM Identity Center permission sets provide reusable role-based permissions with less operational overhead than creating a separate IAM role and user profile for every user. The option simplifies how execution roles and user profiles interact, but it best matches the stated Identity Center and pre-built permissions requirements.

cards.q:
A company has developed a computer vision model. The company needs to deploy the model to a production environment. The company must select the most suitable Amazon SageMaker AI deployment option to meet performance requirements and optimize cost.
The company wants to receive recommendations about what instance types to use for the model.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: Deploy the model to a SageMaker AI real-time inference endpoint. Manually select the instance type based on prior knowledge about instance performance.
Use SageMaker AI Debugger to profile the model after deployment and provide instance type recommendations.
Register the model in the SageMaker Model Registry and use SageMaker Inference Recommender for instance type recommendations.
Configure a SageMaker AI Processing job to benchmark the model across all available instance types. Manually compare the results.
cards.a: C. Register the model in the SageMaker Model Registry and use SageMaker Inference Recommender for instance type recommendations.
cards.explanation: SageMaker Inference Recommender benchmarks registered models and recommends suitable instance types with low operational effort.

cards.q:
A company is using Amazon SageMaker AI to develop an ML model to detect fraudulent transactions. The company's data science team has collected a labeled dataset that contains 1 million transactions. Only 0.1% of the transactions are labeled as fraudulent.
The data science team wants to train an ML model that will detect the fraudulent transactions.
Which approach should the data science team use to address the class imbalance in the dataset?
options: Downsample the majority class to create a more balanced dataset. Train the model on the balanced dataset.
Oversample the minority class by using Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE). Train the model on the balanced dataset.
Use the original unbalanced dataset to train the model. Set a higher weight for the majority class.
Collect more examples of the majority class to create a more balanced dataset. Train the model on the balanced dataset.
cards.a: B. Oversample the minority class by using Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE). Train the model on the balanced dataset.
cards.explanation: SMOTE can create synthetic fraudulent examples from the available minority records and produce a more balanced training set.

cards.q:
A company collects customer data every day. The company ingests the data into Amazon S3 by using a batch process. An ML engineer wants to retrain an ML model weekly based on the new data that has arrived.
The ML engineer needs to set up an automated pipeline to extract, transform, and load (ETL) the data and retrain the model every week with the LEAST operational overhead.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: Use Amazon SageMaker AI Pipelines to define a pipeline that includes ETL steps with AWS Glue and model training steps with SageMaker AI. Schedule the pipeline using Amazon EventBridge Scheduler.
Use AWS Step Functions to orchestrate the ETL process with AWS Glue and the model training process with SageMaker AI Training. Schedule the workflow using an Amazon EventBridge rule.
Deploy an AWS Lambda function that is invoked weekly to start an AWS Glue ETL job. After the Glue job completes, the Lambda function invokes a SageMaker AI training job.
Use Amazon Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow (Amazon MWAA) to orchestrate the ETL process and model training. Define DAGs to handle the weekly data processing and training.
cards.a: B. Use AWS Step Functions to orchestrate the ETL process with AWS Glue and the model training process with SageMaker AI Training. Schedule the workflow using an Amazon EventBridge rule.
cards.explanation: AWS Step Functions directly integrates AWS Glue jobs and SageMaker training jobs, and EventBridge can schedule the workflow weekly.

cards.q:
A company has an ML model in Amazon SageMaker AI. The company must deploy the model to production so it can be queried by other enterprise applications. The company needs to minimize the time the model takes to respond to queries. The company also needs to ensure that the inference infrastructure can scale based on demand.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: Deploy the model to a SageMaker AI real-time inference endpoint with auto scaling.
Deploy the model to a SageMaker AI real-time inference endpoint without auto scaling.
Use SageMaker AI Batch Transform to run inference jobs when needed.
Deploy the model as a serverless inference endpoint in SageMaker AI.
cards.a: A. Deploy the model to a SageMaker AI real-time inference endpoint with auto scaling.
cards.explanation: A real-time endpoint minimizes online latency, while auto scaling adjusts provisioned capacity to demand.

cards.q:
A company is using Amazon SageMaker AI to deploy a new recommendation model for its ecommerce website. The model must use data from all client website interactions as input.
Traffic is variable throughout the day. The company needs to create an inference endpoint for the model.
Which type of inference endpoint will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
options: Batch transform inference endpoint
Asynchronous inference endpoint
Real-time inference endpoint
Serverless inference endpoint
cards.a: D. Serverless inference endpoint
cards.explanation: Serverless inference avoids idle instance charges for intermittent or unpredictable traffic, making it the most cost-effective listed endpoint.

cards.q:
A company runs an Amazon SageMaker AI domain in a public subnet of a newly created VPC. The network is configured properly, and ML engineers can access the SageMaker AI domain.
Recently, the company discovered suspicious traffic to the domain from a specific IP address. The company needs to block traffic from the specific IP address.
Which update to the network configuration will meet this requirement?
options: Create a security group inbound rule to deny traffic from the specific IP address. Assign the security group to the domain.
Create a network ACL inbound rule to deny traffic from the specific IP address. Assign the rule to the default network ACL for the subnet where the domain is located.
Create a shadow variant for the domain. Configure SageMaker Inference Recommender to send traffic from the specific IP address to the shadow endpoint.
Create a VPC route table to deny inbound traffic from the specific IP address. Assign the route table to the domain.
cards.a: B. Create a network ACL inbound rule to deny traffic from the specific IP address. Assign the rule to the default network ACL for the subnet where the domain is located.
cards.explanation: Network ACLs support explicit deny rules, unlike security groups, and can block the source IP at the subnet boundary.

cards.q:
A company's ML engineer is creating a classification model. The ML engineer explores the dataset and discovers that the target variable is a categorical variable that contains 10 different values. The ML engineer needs to encode the target variable before training the model.
Which encoding strategy should the ML engineer use?
options: Binary encoding
Label encoding
One-hot encoding
Tokenization
cards.a: B. Label encoding
cards.explanation: Multiclass target labels are normally mapped to integer class IDs. One-hot encoding is more commonly applied to input features.

cards.q:
An ML engineer wants to use Amazon SageMaker AI to prepare data for training. During exploratory data analysis, the ML engineer notices that several categorical features are missing values.
How can the ML engineer use SageMaker AI to solve this problem?
options: Use SageMaker Clarify to impute categorical features with the mean value.
Use SageMaker Clarity to impute categorical features with the mode value.
Use SageMaker Data Wrangler to impute categorical features with the mean value.
Use SageMaker Data Wrangler to impute categorical features with the mode value.
cards.a: D. Use SageMaker Data Wrangler to impute categorical features with the mode value.
cards.explanation: SageMaker Data Wrangler supports missing-value transformations, and mode imputation is appropriate for categorical features.

cards.q:
A company stores user clickstream data in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company wants to use the data to train a recommendation model. To reduce computational costs, the company wants to preprocess only the relevant features from the dataset and eliminate redundant features.
Which solution will address the redundant features with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: Use Amazon SageMaker AI Feature Store to discover and deduplicate the features.
Use Amazon SageMaker AI Data Wrangler to analyze and reduce the dataset features.
Use an Amazon SageMaker AI Processing job with a custom Python script to eliminate redundant features.
Use Amazon SageMaker AI Clarify to identify and exclude redundant features from the dataset.
cards.a: B. Use Amazon SageMaker AI Data Wrangler to analyze and reduce the dataset features.
cards.explanation: SageMaker Data Wrangler provides managed analyses and transformations for finding correlations and reducing redundant features.

cards.q:
A music streaming company constantly streams song play data from its users. The company wants to use ML to provide real-time recommendations for users based on their listening activity.
The company needs a solution that processes data as it arrives to generate personalized recommendations with minimal latency.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to collect and process the streaming data. Use Amazon SageMaker AI for real-time ML inference to generate recommendations.
Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to buffer incoming song data. Use an AWS Lambda function to process and generate recommendations.
Use Amazon S3 to store all incoming song data and run a daily batch ML job to generate recommendations.
Use Amazon DynamoDB Streams to capture the incoming song play data and run an ML model to generate recommendations.
cards.a: A. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to collect and process the streaming data. Use Amazon SageMaker AI for real-time ML inference to generate recommendations.
cards.explanation: Kinesis Data Streams handles continuous events, and a SageMaker real-time endpoint provides low-latency recommendation inference.

cards.q:
A hospital is using an ML model to validate x-ray results. The hospital runs a nightly batch job that processes medical images and generates validation reports. The hospital stores the images in Amazon S3.
The model requires GPUs for efficient inference. The processing runs on Amazon SageMaker AI.
Which solution will run the batch job MOST cost-effectively?
options: Use a SageMaker AI real-time inference endpoint with GPU-based instances. Schedule the batch job to run at night.
Use SageMaker AI asynchronous inference with GPU-based instances.
Use SageMaker AI Batch Transform with GPU-based instances.
Use SageMaker AI Batch Transform with GPU-based Spot Instances.
cards.a: C. Use SageMaker AI Batch Transform with GPU-based instances.
cards.explanation: SageMaker Batch Transform fits nightly S3-based GPU inference and avoids an always-on endpoint. Batch Transform does not provide managed Spot Instances.

cards.q:
A company needs to ingest data from data sources into a data lake to train ML models. The data sources include relational databases, NoSQL databases, and data streams.
The company needs the LEAST operational overhead solution for data ingestion and data processing.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: Use AWS Glue to connect to data sources, transform, and load data into Amazon S3.
Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to replicate data from relational databases. Use AWS Lambda to process data from NoSQL databases and data streams.
Use Amazon Data Firehose to ingest data from all data sources.
Use AWS Batch to schedule data ingestion jobs from all data sources.
cards.a: A. Use AWS Glue to connect to data sources, transform, and load data into Amazon S3.
cards.explanation: AWS Glue provides managed connectors and ETL for supported databases and streams, then writes transformed data to Amazon S3.

cards.q:
An ML engineer is using Amazon SageMaker Canvas to build a model to predict customer churn. The ML engineer wants to understand how different feature values affect the model's predictions.
Which SageMaker Canvas feature should the ML engineer use?
options: Bias detection
Model explainability
Confusion matrix
SHAP values
cards.a: D. SHAP values
cards.explanation: SHAP values quantify how each feature value contributes to a model prediction.

cards.q:
A company has built, trained, and tuned two new ML models for binary classification. The company wants to use the model that produces the most accurate results for all data subgroups. The company's ML team needs to audit model metrics for bias.
Which solution will meet this requirement?
options: Use Amazon SageMaker AI Data Wrangler to generate a data analysis report for each model that shows insights about class imbalances.
Use Amazon SageMaker AI Model Monitor to detect data and model drift for both models after deployment.
Use Amazon SageMaker AI Clarify to generate bias reports for both models.
Use Amazon SageMaker AI Experiments to create a comparison chart of the metrics from both models.
cards.a: C. Use Amazon SageMaker AI Clarify to generate bias reports for both models.
cards.explanation: SageMaker Clarify computes bias metrics across facets and subgroups. Drift monitoring and experiment charts do not perform this audit.

cards.q:
A bank needs to use Amazon SageMaker AI to create an ML model that predicts the credit score of a customer. The bank also needs to explain the model predictions. The bank must ensure that the ML model is free of bias by running a bias analysis before the model is trained.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: Configure an Amazon SageMaker AI Clarify bias analysis job with the training dataset and label mapping. Run the job before training begins.
Configure a SageMaker AI Clarify processing job with the training dataset and label mapping. Run the job before training begins.
Configure an Amazon SageMaker AI Debugger analysis job with the training dataset. Run the job before training begins.
Configure a SageMaker AI Data Wrangler job with the training dataset and label mapping. Run the job before training begins.
cards.a: B. Configure a SageMaker AI Clarify processing job with the training dataset and label mapping. Run the job before training begins.
cards.explanation: SageMaker Clarify performs pre-training bias analysis through a processing job configured with the dataset, label, and facet information.

cards.q:
A company is preparing data to train a new ML model. The data is stored in a database table that has 100 columns and 1 million rows. The company needs to remove features that are highly correlated with each other before training the model.
Which solution will meet this requirement MOST efficiently?
options: Use Pearson's correlation coefficient to measure the linear correlation between columns. Remove columns that exceed the correlation threshold.
Use a variance inflation factor (VIF) analysis to identify highly correlated columns. Remove columns that exceed the VIF threshold.
Use Principal Component Analysis (PCA) to reduce the number of dimensions.
Use feature importance scores from a decision tree model to identify and remove the least important features.
cards.a: A. Use Pearson's correlation coefficient to measure the linear correlation between columns. Remove columns that exceed the correlation threshold.
cards.explanation: A Pearson correlation matrix directly and efficiently identifies highly correlated column pairs. VIF targets broader multicollinearity and requires auxiliary regressions.

cards.q:
An ML engineer is building a model to predict house and apartment prices. The model uses three features: Square Meters, Price, and Age of Building. The dataset has 10,000 data rows. The data includes data points for one large mansion and one extremely small apartment.
The ML engineer must perform preprocessing on the dataset to ensure that the model produces accurate predictions for the vast majority of houses and apartments.
Which preprocessing step should the ML engineer perform?
options: Remove the outlier data points for the large mansion and the extremely small apartment from the dataset.
Apply min-max normalization to scale the features to a range of [0, 1].
Apply standard normalization (Z-score) to the features.
Apply log transformation to the features to reduce the impact of extreme values.
cards.a: A. Remove the outlier data points for the large mansion and the extremely small apartment from the dataset.
cards.explanation: Removing two verified extreme outliers protects predictions for the stated majority better than scaling alone. Legitimate extreme properties should still be investigated before removal.

cards.q:
A company is developing an ML model by using Amazon SageMaker AI Studio. The ML engineers want to use GPU instances to improve training performance. The ML engineers also want to maintain the ability to restart the model training without losing progress.
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
options: Use On-Demand GPU Instances.
Use Spot GPU Instances with checkpointing enabled.
Use Reserved GPU Instances.
Use Dedicated Hosts with GPU instances.
cards.a: B. Use Spot GPU Instances with checkpointing enabled.
cards.explanation: Managed Spot GPU training reduces cost, while checkpointing allows recovery after an interruption.

cards.q:
A company is using an Amazon SageMaker AI ML model that is deployed on a real-time inference endpoint for product recommendations. The company is concerned about the increased response time for requests when new instances launch to handle high demand.
Which solution will minimize the response time for new instances?
options: Enable SageMaker AI automatic scaling with step scaling policies.
Configure SageMaker AI endpoint pre-warming.
Use SageMaker AI inference pipelines to distribute load.
Enable SageMaker AI multi-model endpoints.
cards.a: B. Configure SageMaker AI endpoint pre-warming.
cards.explanation: Inference pipelines chain containers and do not reduce instance startup latency. Endpoint pre-warming appears to be the intended option, although proactive capacity or a higher minimum instance count would be the standard approach.

cards.q:
A company uses ML models to predict whether transactions are fraudulent. The company has deployed the models on Amazon SageMaker AI real-time inference endpoints. A data scientist notices that the model performance has degraded over time.
The data scientist suspects that the input data has changed since the models were trained. The data scientist needs to identify the root cause.
Which solution will meet this requirement?
options: Use Amazon SageMaker AI Debugger to capture anomalous data inputs.
Use Amazon SageMaker AI Clarify to analyze feature importance.
Use Amazon SageMaker AI Model Monitor to monitor the endpoint and detect data drift.
Use Amazon SageMaker AI Experiments to compare the current model with the original model.
cards.a: C. Use Amazon SageMaker AI Model Monitor to monitor the endpoint and detect data drift.
cards.explanation: SageMaker Model Monitor compares endpoint inputs against a baseline to detect distribution changes. SageMaker Experiments cannot diagnose production drift by itself.

cards.q:
A recommendation model uses ML and calls an Amazon SageMaker AI endpoint to retrieve real-time recommendations. The model is updated frequently because of new user interaction data. An ML engineer must implement a solution to deploy model updates without affecting the user experience.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: Configure a blue/green deployment strategy for the SageMaker AI endpoint.
Use Amazon CloudFront to cache the recommendation responses and reduce the impact of model updates.
Retrain the model by using SageMaker AI Pipelines and automatically deploy to the existing endpoint.
Use SageMaker AI multi-model endpoints to host multiple versions of the model.
cards.a: A. Configure a blue/green deployment strategy for the SageMaker AI endpoint.
cards.explanation: A blue-green deployment creates a replacement fleet, shifts traffic safely, and supports rollback without interrupting users.

cards.q:
A hospital wants to predict patient outcomes for the coming year. An ML engineer must improve several existing ML models that currently perform poorly.

Select the correct regularization method from the following list to improve each model. Select each regularization method one time, more than one time, or not at all. (Choose three.)
cards.a:
Linear regression model whose coefficients should shrink but not become zero: L2 regularization (Ridge)
Polynomial regression model with irrelevant polynomial terms that should be eliminated: L1 regularization (Lasso)
Logistic regression model with highly correlated features to eliminate redundant predictors: L1 regularization (Lasso)
cards.explanation: L2 shrinks coefficients without normally zeroing them. L1 can remove irrelevant polynomial terms and select among redundant predictors.

prompts.label: Linear regression model whose coefficients should shrink but not become zero
Polynomial regression model with irrelevant polynomial terms that should be eliminated
Logistic regression model with highly correlated features to eliminate redundant predictors

cards.q:
An ML engineer has trained an ML model by using Amazon SageMaker AI. The ML engineer needs to deploy the model to a SageMaker AI endpoint and make it available to internal applications. The internal applications run in private subnets. The ML engineer must ensure that the traffic between the applications and the SageMaker AI endpoint does not traverse the public internet.
Which solution will meet this requirement?
options: Deploy the model to a SageMaker AI real-time inference endpoint. Create a VPC with a public subnet. Route all traffic through the public subnet.

Deploy the model to a SageMaker AI real-time inference endpoint. Create an interface VPC endpoint for the SageMaker AI Runtime service. Configure the VPC endpoint in the private subnet where the internal applications run.
Deploy the model to a SageMaker AI real-time inference endpoint. Use AWS PrivateLink to create a gateway VPC endpoint for the SageMaker AI Runtime service.
Deploy the model to a SageMaker AI serverless inference endpoint. Use Amazon CloudFront to route requests from the private subnet to the serverless endpoint.
cards.a: B. Deploy the model to a SageMaker AI real-time inference endpoint. Create an interface VPC endpoint for the SageMaker AI Runtime service. Configure the VPC endpoint in the private subnet where the internal applications run.
cards.explanation: A SageMaker Runtime interface VPC endpoint uses AWS PrivateLink so private-subnet applications avoid the public internet.

cards.q:
An ML engineer wants to use Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler to process a large dataset for an ML model. The ML engineer wants to apply several transformations to the data, including normalization, one-hot encoding, and handling of missing values. The ML engineer also wants to save the processing result to Amazon S3 so that a team can access the data.
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
options: Process the dataset in SageMaker Data Wrangler. Export the SageMaker Data Wrangler flow to a SageMaker AI Pipeline and run it on a cluster of on-demand instances.
Process the dataset in SageMaker Data Wrangler. Export the SageMaker Data Wrangler flow to a SageMaker AI processing job and run it on a cluster of Spot Instances.
Process the dataset in SageMaker Data Wrangler. Export the SageMaker Data Wrangler flow to an AWS Glue job and run it on a cluster of Spot Instances.
Process the dataset in SageMaker Data Wrangler. Export the SageMaker Data Wrangler flow to an Amazon EMR cluster and run it on a cluster of Spot Instances.
cards.a: A. Process the dataset in SageMaker Data Wrangler. Export the SageMaker Data Wrangler flow to a SageMaker AI Pipeline and run it on a cluster of on-demand instances.
cards.explanation: A Data Wrangler flow can be exported to SageMaker Pipelines and run with managed processing. Standard SageMaker Processing jobs do not support Managed Spot, so option B is invalid.

cards.q:
An ML engineer is training a text generation model on a cluster of Amazon EC2 instances by using a deep learning framework. The training is distributed across multiple nodes. The ML engineer notices that the training speed is limited because of frequent synchronization between nodes.
Which solution will address this performance issue MOST efficiently?
options: Increase the number of nodes to spread the computation.
Use larger instances with more memory to reduce data transfer.
Implement gradient compression to reduce the communication overhead during synchronization.
Use Amazon Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) to increase network bandwidth between nodes.
cards.a: C. Implement gradient compression to reduce the communication overhead during synchronization.
cards.explanation: Gradient compression reduces the bytes exchanged during synchronization and directly addresses communication overhead between training nodes.

cards.q:
A company uses an NFS-based data store to store data for ML training. The data store is on premises. To move data to an Amazon S3 bucket for ML training on Amazon SageMaker AI, the company transfers the data by using AWS Storage Gateway File Gateway.
The data transfer process is slow and sometimes results in incomplete transfers. The company needs to improve the reliability and speed of data transfer to Amazon S3 while minimizing operational overhead.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: Configure AWS DataSync to transfer data from the NFS data store to the S3 bucket. Schedule transfers to run at regular intervals.
Configure AWS Transfer Family with SFTP to transfer files from the NFS data store to the S3 bucket.
Configure an AWS Direct Connect connection to improve the speed and reliability of data transfer from the NFS data store.
Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to stream data from the NFS data store to the S3 bucket in real time.
cards.a: A. Configure AWS DataSync to transfer data from the NFS data store to the S3 bucket. Schedule transfers to run at regular intervals.
cards.explanation: AWS DataSync natively supports reliable, incremental NFS-to-S3 transfers with verification, retries, scheduling, and low operational overhead.

cards.q:
A company needs to analyze a large dataset that is stored in Amazon S3 in Apache Parquet format. The company wants to use one-hot encoding for some of the columns.
The company needs a no-code solution to transform the data. The solution must store the transformed data back to the same S3 bucket for model training.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: Configure an AWS Glue DataBrew project. Use the project to transform the data and output the results to the S3 bucket.
Use Amazon SageMaker AI Data Wrangler to analyze and transform the data. Export the results to the S3 bucket.
Build a custom AWS Lambda function that reads data from S3, transforms the data, and writes the results back to S3.
Use Amazon EMR with an Apache Spark job to transform the data and write the results back to S3.
cards.a: A. Configure an AWS Glue DataBrew project. Use the project to transform the data and output the results to the S3 bucket.
cards.explanation: AWS Glue DataBrew can read Parquet, apply a no-code one-hot encoding recipe, and write the transformed data to Amazon S3.

cards.q:
A company wants to migrate ML models from an on-premises environment to the AWS Cloud. The company wants to host the models on Amazon SageMaker AI. The models are implemented by using various open source ML frameworks. The company has thousands of models and wants to reduce the operational complexity of hosting them.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: Create one SageMaker AI endpoint for each model.
Use SageMaker AI multi-model endpoints to host multiple models with the same ML framework on a single endpoint.
Use SageMaker AI model containers to host all models by using a single container image.
Use SageMaker AI multi-model endpoints with a custom inference container to host all models on a single endpoint.
cards.a: D. Use SageMaker AI multi-model endpoints with a custom inference container to host all models on a single endpoint.
cards.explanation: A custom multi-model inference container can implement loaders for several frameworks behind fewer endpoints, reducing fleet management overhead.

cards.q:
A company uses an Amazon QuickSight dashboard to track business metrics about an ML model deployed to a SageMaker AI real-time endpoint. Recently, the team noticed that the model's predictions have become less accurate over time.
An ML engineer suspects model drift due to changes in user behavior patterns. The ML engineer wants to monitor the model for drift and receive automated alerts.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: Create a CloudWatch alarm based on the endpoint invocations metric to monitor model drift.
Schedule a regular SageMaker AI Clarify job to compute feature attribution and detect drift.
Set up SageMaker AI Model Monitor with the Data Quality and Model Quality monitoring schedule. Configure Amazon CloudWatch alarms to notify when drift is detected.
Implement a custom drift detection solution by using AWS Lambda and Amazon CloudWatch.
cards.a: C. Set up SageMaker AI Model Monitor with the Data Quality and Model Quality monitoring schedule. Configure Amazon CloudWatch alarms to notify when drift is detected.
cards.explanation: SageMaker Model Monitor data-quality and model-quality schedules detect drift, and CloudWatch alarms automate notification.

cards.q:
An ML engineer is using Amazon QuickSight anomaly detection to identify outliers in business data for a retail company. The ML engineer configured the anomaly detection to detect anomalies in sales data. Now the ML engineer needs to set up automated alerts when the anomaly detection finds significant anomalies.
Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule to detect anomalies in QuickSight and send notifications by using Amazon SNS.
Set up a QuickSight threshold alert for the anomaly detection result. Configure the alert to notify users by email when anomalies are detected.
Configure an AWS Lambda function that runs on a schedule to query the QuickSight anomaly detection results and notify users through Amazon SNS.
Set up an Amazon CloudWatch alarm on the QuickSight anomaly detection metric to send notifications when anomalies are detected.
cards.a: B. Set up a QuickSight threshold alert for the anomaly detection result. Configure the alert to notify users by email when anomalies are detected.
cards.explanation: Native QuickSight alerts provide the lowest-overhead notification path for significant anomalies.

cards.q:
A company runs its ML workflows on an on-premises computing cluster because of concerns about data privacy. The company wants to use Amazon SageMaker AI for ML training while ensuring that the training data does not leave the on-premises environment.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: Use AWS Direct Connect to connect the on-premises cluster to AWS. Store data on AWS and run SageMaker AI training jobs.
Use SageMaker AI Training Compiler to train models in a cloud environment with the data fully encrypted.
Use Amazon SageMaker AI Edge Manager to deploy and train models on the on-premises infrastructure.
Use SageMaker AI training jobs with SageMaker AI local mode so that training is performed locally on on-premises hardware.
cards.a: D. Use SageMaker AI training jobs with SageMaker AI local mode so that training is performed locally on on-premises hardware.
cards.explanation: SageMaker local mode runs compatible containers on local hardware, allowing data to remain on premises. Training Compiler still performs training in the cloud.

cards.q:
An ML engineer needs to run intensive model training jobs each month that can take 48 to 72 hours to complete. The ML engineer needs to optimize the costs of running these jobs.
Which instance purchasing option will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
options: Purchase Reserved Instances with a partial upfront payment.
Purchase On-Demand Instances with no commitment.
Purchase Amazon SageMaker AI Savings Plans.
Purchase Spot Instances that use automated checkpoints.
cards.a: D. Purchase Spot Instances that use automated checkpoints.
cards.explanation: Spot capacity plus checkpoints is the most economical listed choice for periodic, restartable training jobs that run for several days.

cards.q:
An ML engineer needs to use Amazon SageMaker hyperparameter tuning to reduce the training time for an ML model.

Select and order the correct steps from the following list to meet this requirement. Each step should be selected one time or not at all. (Select and order three.)
cards.a:
Step 1: Choose Hyperband tuning and decrease the number of parameters.
Step 2: Retrain the model.
Step 3: Evaluate the change in training time.
cards.explanation: Hyperband stops weak configurations early, and reducing the search space lowers work. The changed training run must execute before its elapsed time can be evaluated.

choices: Choose Bayesian optimization and increase the number of parameters.
Choose Hyperband tuning and decrease the number of parameters.
Choose random search and use a random seed of -1.
Deploy the model to a SageMaker endpoint.
Evaluate the change in training time.

Step 2
Step 3

cards.q:
A company develops an ML model to classify products. The model uses textual data and visual data to classify the products into a hierarchical taxonomy. An ML engineer must use specific strategies to enhance the model's accuracy and handle class imbalances.

Select the correct strategy from the following list for each use case. Select each strategy one time. (Choose five.)
cards.a:
Evaluate predictions with tolerance for broader category matches: Fallback metric
Balance the training data by increasing the presence of minority categories: General oversampling
Enhance the model's ability to recognize nested structures within product categories: Hierarchical loss
Enhance textual data representation for underrepresented categories: Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) for text
Standard loss function for multi-class classification: Categorical cross-entropy
cards.explanation: The mappings align tolerant evaluation, oversampling, hierarchical loss, vector-space SMOTE, and categorical cross-entropy with their respective use cases.

choices: Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) for text

prompts.label: Evaluate predictions with tolerance for broader category matches
Balance the training data by increasing the presence of minority categories
